key_insight: Detonation-sprayed hydroxyapatite coatings improved titanium wear resistance, with the best friction behavior and lowest wear volume at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 3.0 and 3.3.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing the detonation-spray gas ratio could improve the wear durability of titanium implants in physiological environments.
method: Deposit hydroxyapatite on Grade 2 titanium at O₂/C₂H₂ ratios of 2.6–3.7.
Identify coating phases using X-ray diffraction.
Evaluate friction and wear under dry conditions and in Ringer’s solution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports predominantly hydroxyapatite with partial α-tricalcium phosphate formation and significantly greater wear resistance than uncoated titanium, but provides no numerical wear results.
watch_item: Improved osseointegration and long-term implant reliability require biological and durability validation beyond the reported tribological tests.
paper_title: STUDY OF TRIBOLOGICAL PROPERTIES OF BIOCOATINGS BY DETONATION SPRAYING METHOD
